To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a customer with an ESS can save 5–7% of the monthly electricity bill when compared to a non-ESS customer and that the savings are higher when a supply charge is implemented.
a customer with an ESS can reduce peak net demand by 46–64%, reduce net demand fluctuations by up to 50%, and increase solar PV self-consume by up to 39% by scheduling the charge/discharge of an ESS.

the CO-based charge/discharge scheduling reduces (1) peak customer net demand, (2) customer reliance on the grid, and (3), when a supply charge is introduced, the amount of solar PV power that must be curtailed.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a CO-based ESS scheduling algorithm for behind-the-meter distributed energy resources that can reduce peak net demand, mitigate net demand fluctuations, and increase the self-consumption rate of locally generated solar PV.

the development of a new ESS charge/discharge scheduling method that can be implemented by a customer to minimize electricity costs, reduce the peak net demand, and reduce power fluctuations of the net demand profile.

the optimal scheduling of behind-the-meter EES systems to minimize electricity bills, reduce net demand fluctuations, and mitigate reverse power flows in the distribution grid by way of increasing solar PV energy self-consumptions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed CO-based scheduling algorithm can be a cost-effective tool for ESS owners to minimize their monthly electricity expenses and reduce their reliance on the grid.
the proposed algorithm provides an effective means for ESS owners to minimize monthly electricity expenses and maximize the self-consumption and utilization of local solar PV power.
the CO-based charge/discharge scheduling of ESSs is a cost-effective way to manage behind-the-meter solar PV generation and load.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a novel CO-based scheduling algorithm that can be used by ESS owners to minimize their monthly electricity expenses and maximize the use of local solar PV power.
the CO-based charge/discharge algorithm provides a cost effective and reliable method for scheduling behind-the-meter distributed energy storage systems.

the CO-based algorithm provides a significant reduction in the monthly electricity expenses for ESS owners, and the introduction of a supply charge tariff can be a viable option to reduce the reverse power flow from solar PV systems to the distribution grid.

ESSs are a cost-effective means to reduce net demand fluctuations, reduce the reliance of customers on the grid, and increase the solar PV self-con- sumption.
